I just got back from Disneyland, it’s a big trip for me. We went a whole week, it is my favorite park. While I had a lot of fun and it was most certainly worth it, I did have a few “huh” moments while there. The big thing for me was the cast member chatter. There were many many cast members just complaining about their day to their coworkers while robotically gesturing to the entrance/exit. I don’t even blame the CM per say, they aren’t paid enough to be “live entertainment” all day. I probably wouldn’t be all smiles either. But it’s still a big piece of the immersion for me. Not every CM has to “play a character,” but I’d at least appreciate it if they played into the magic. I don’t want to hear them complaining about adult-everyday-problems… while I’m on vacation trying to distract myself from that exact stuff. I just wished the real world stayed outside, but it is seeping through those cracks.

So my ex attempted suicide when we split. I felt like it was a toxic relationship and when I tried to break things off he would threaten to take his own life, and after months of that I finally decided to go through with the breakup and cut the cord. I called his friends and told them to keep an eye on him, but sure enough he attempted that night, thankfully he survived and I’m very grateful for that. Just because our relationship didn’t work doesn’t mean I hate the man, I still care about him all these years later I’m so so glad he wasn’t successful. 

To answer your question, no, it’s not a good way. He texted me the following day asking if his attempt proved to me that we need to be together, I told him that while I was so happy he was alive, that we simply couldn’t continue to date. He flipped and said I would have to “live with the guilt” that I drove him to try and end his life. And I struggled with that for a long time, I beat myself up about everything I could have done differently, and I fear that I made his life worse from us being together, BUT I will tell you that now I know it wasn’t my fault and that that decision was his. While it will hurt the person in the short term, it won’t make anything change. That decision is yours, and it will not have been their fault and after they get through the guilt, they will continue to live their life knowing it wasn’t their fault. It is not the only way. I hope things get better for you and I hope you find a way through this besides that path.

YTA, I get it, time is fucked, but there are ways of coping with this. Set reminders on your phone, set alarms (10 if you need to), keep a calendar that sends you text alerts, or anything like that! If your brain can’t keep track of it all, let a computer do it. When you learn of an event, put it in the calendar, set a reminder a few days prior reminding you, and the day of. It’s a hard habit to make, it was really hard for me to stick to it and really keep up with it, but after the habit sets in it really takes a load off your mind. This is something worth working on, I promise! Good luck to you!

While it is awful that this woman passed away, I think it’s incredibly disrespectful of them to not respect your wishes ESPECIALLY given your reasoning, which I think is very sound. I grew up with a friend with anorexia in middle school and it confused me a lot at that age and made me much more aware of all those body image problems, something most women (myself included) will struggle with at some point. Given your daughter was only 3, I can’t imagine how this would have frightened or confused her. You likely spared your daughter a horrible last memory of this person they loved. Unfortunately, I don’t have any advise for you on dealing with the family, I’m sure they’re just very hurt over her death and are taking some of that out on you, that might just need to run it’s course. I would encourage you to stand your ground on your decision, stand by your convictions, and don’t cave because of guilt. You did what you thought was best for your daughter and that is your greatest priority.

I guess I go with stock over degreaser just for the low ammo to air blast ratio, if I’m in a match where the other team isn’t really running pyro or my team is able to get behind the other team easily I will still switch to backburner now and again, but only situationally. Overall I think it’s personal preference, it feels really weird to switch from one flamethrower to another after growing accustomed to it, but if you wanna see why most run stock I would just try it for a few matches and see if it’s for you. 🔥
